scope: Isolated in-memory comparator evidence, not complete Nix evaluation speed.
method: Eight balanced scalar/candidate passes per case; all passes retained. Each row times set construction and four complete 89,979-query traversals, recording their average lookup time. Git order and fixed seed 1729 shuffled order. Equivalence validation precedes timing; no cache eviction. Source, binaries, logs, input and SHA-256 manifest archived read-only without rerunning timing.

both_candidates.actual_path_sorted_sequences: exact element-by-element equality for both set sizes
both_candidates.actual_path_lower_bound_results: exact equality for all89979 queries at both set sizes
both_candidates.timed_output_checksums: order and lookup checksums agree in every recorded case

validation.limits: Standalone finite byte fixtures include some noncanonical strings; they verify the scalar transformation on a wider byte-string domain. Production CanonPath tests are separate and are not claimed by these archived runs.

decisions.component_lexicographic: rejected because every measured case is slower
decisions.equal_uint64_prefix_skip: accepted as an integration candidate because every measured case is faster; only equality skips words, scalar separator-first order decides inequalities

limits: This isolates in-memory set construction and lookup, not Nix evaluation, raw filesystem traversal, store effects, or any complete URI benchmark.
One architecture, compiler and CPU were measured; there is no cold-cache or cross-machine inference.
The benchmark uses a standalone Path representation and copies of the comparator/Iterator, not the linked Nix CanonPath implementation.
Raw CSV lookup values aggregate four inner iterations; individual inner-iteration times were not captured.
All measured cases and passes are retained; timing was not rerun during archival.
